hook: Group brainstorming doesn't work. Here's why.
facts: In *1953*, an ad man named Osborn popularized group brainstorming.
In *1987*, Diehl and Stroebe compared groups with people working alone.
Solo thinkers produced *more ideas* once their lists were pooled.
The culprit is *production blocking*: you wait your turn and forget your idea.
title: Psychology Facts
